note.backdrop: Wednesday closed split: the S&P 500 -0.23% to 7,323.63, its fifth loss in a row and below its 200-day average; the Dow -1.11% (-561 points), dragged by UnitedHealth, Chevron and Caterpillar; the Nasdaq +0.42% (Motley Fool; StockTitan citing CNBC). The Fed's October minutes said nearly all officials judged further rate increases likely appropriate; the dollar reached a 19-month high and the 10-year yield eased two basis points to 5.10% (Motley Fool). After the close, Anthropic priced its offering at $83 a share, above its $70-$78 range: 980 million shares, about $81 billion raised, about $1.5 trillion in value, trading Thursday on Nasdaq as ANT (AP on Yahoo; StockTitan from its SEC filing). Stock funds rose after hours: SPY +0.7%, QQQ +1.4%. The check's driver lines after the close are wrong again: oil -4.5% and gold -3.6% are measured from Tuesday's bars, not Wednesday's. December WTI settled at $83.26 (-3.2% on the day) and January at $82.31; after hours January is $82.16, -0.2%. Gold's December contract closed at $3,741.90 (-3.2%) and is $3,727.00 after hours, -0.4%; the futures line's +0.4% is +0.7% from Wednesday's close. Only 2 stocks are outside their 9-in-10 range after hours. Outside the scan, Hyster-Yale fell 41.1% the day it proposed $125 million of convertible notes and amended its credit agreement to permit 'certain financing transactions' (its 8-K; StockTitan); a $125 million convertible does not by itself explain a fall that size, so the cause of its size is not established.

read.says: S&P 500 -0.24% to 7,323, below its 200-day average; Nasdaq +0.42%; Dow -1.11%; gold -3.51% to $3,728.60; 10-year yield 5.10%; UnitedHealth -10.21%, Humana -12.98% on the Medicare Advantage audit proposal; TJX +8.05%; Amazon +3.82% on its Anthropic stake; Fed minutes: nearly all officials see further hikes as likely needed; dollar at a 19-month high; Walmart reports Thursday.

At the close SPY -0.31%, QQQ +0.39%, DIA -1.10%, IWM +0.40%; Nvidia closed -2.89%; BellRing +24.07%; Hyster-Yale -41.07% the day it proposed convertible notes; tariff refunds were $0.50 of Target's $2.65 EPS; after hours QQQ +1.38%, SPY +0.72%, Palo Alto +9.08% after raising its revenue forecast; Anthropic's filing gives an $83 price.

Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above a $70-$78 range, valuing it at about $1.5 trillion; 980 million shares (about 956 million sold by the company), about $81 billion raised, the largest IPO on record; trading Thursday on Nasdaq as ANT; it reports $6.2 billion of debt and commitments of about $900 billion for computing over coming years, $70 billion in the next 12 months.
Hyster-Yale amended its credit agreement to permit certain financing transactions and announced a proposed private offering of $125 million of convertible senior notes due 2031.

Red Robin's third quarter: comparable restaurant revenue +3.9% (traffic -1.7%, check +5.6%), adjusted EBITDA $7.3 million; about $100 million borrowed and total liquidity of about $29.5 million ($23.8 million cash); fourth-quarter outlook: comparable revenue about +2.75%, adjusted EBITDA about $6.0 million, updated for refranchising.

Magnera's fourth quarter: net sales $851 million, operating loss $90 million including $106 million of impairments, adjusted EBITDA +8% on a better price-cost spread; volumes down 4%; fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA $378 million.

Ardent Health priced a secondary offering of 8,000,000 shares by affiliates of Equity Group Investments and Ventas at $14.50, with a concurrent repurchase of 1,500,000 shares; expected to close on November 19, 2026.

singles.beneath: In proportion: a $150 million company with about $100 million borrowed and about $29.5 million of total liquidity, earning about $6-7 million of EBITDA a quarter before rent and interest. Thin liquidity is what a weak quarter threatens; my reading is that the fall prices that risk, not the quarter itself.
singles.cause: Red Robin fell 17.5% after hours on its third quarter: comparable restaurant revenue +3.9% but traffic -1.7%, adjusted EBITDA $7.3 million, and a fourth-quarter outlook of about $6.0 million of adjusted EBITDA (its release; Zacks counts an 11.9% revenue miss).

singles.beneath: In proportion: the equity is worth $428 million beside $1.9 billion of debt and $280 million of cash, so the business is worth about $2.05 billion. The guide's middle, $400 million, is 5.8% above $378 million; at the same multiple the business would gain about $120 million, all of it the equity's, about 28%. The +15% is about half of that: the leverage explains why a modest guide moves the stock this much (my arithmetic).
singles.cause: Magnera rose 15.0% after hours on fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA up 8% and a fiscal 2027 guide of $390-$410 million against $378 million in fiscal 2026 (its release; StockTitan).

singles.beneath: The company is spending this year's profit growth on up to 12 new campuses; flat EBITDA for a year of building is the cost of that plan, and the market priced the wait.
singles.cause: Universal Technical Institute fell 8.6% after hours: fourth-quarter earnings missed and its fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA guide of $100-$106 million compares with $102.0 million in fiscal 2026, including about $35 million of costs for new campuses and programs (Investing.com; StockTitan).

themes.beneath: In proportion: Humana closed 13.0% lower after -3.6% on Tuesday, about 16% in two days; UnitedHealth about 15% (-5.2% then -10.2%), about $55 billion of value on a $372 billion company before Tuesday. That is about six years of CMS's estimated $9 billion a year for the whole industry, lost by one company: the market is pricing a lasting cut to Medicare Advantage margins, not one repayment (my inference). The proposal is open for comment to Jan 19, 2027, and the earlier rule is on appeal.
themes.cause: The Medicare Advantage audit proposal (CRUSH, Nov 16) is the only reported cause (Motley Fool). Wednesday's closes (the bank's daily bars): Humana -13.0%, UnitedHealth -10.2%, Elevance -7.6%, Oscar -7.6%, Centene -7.0%, Molina -6.6%, CVS -5.2%, Cigna -3.0%; the Medicare Advantage care groups agilon -21.4%, Alignment -11.8%, Clover -11.8%. After hours they barely moved (UnitedHealth -0.3%, Humana -0.5%).
themes.mechanism: Same as at midday: the companies most tied to Medicare Advantage fell most, Cigna least. The midday fall deepened into the close with no new report I could find, so the last leg is selling, not news; that is my inference.

themes.watch: Whether any insurer quantifies its exposure; whether the group steadies Thursday without news. Three days of falls with no new information is where a reversal or a fourth leg tells whether the market overshot.

themes.beneath: Two up days of 10-15% for the smaller names, before and after a number: the group moved first on a speech, then got the confirmation. Application software kept falling into the close (HubSpot -5.2%, Atlassian -4.2%, Adobe -4.0%, Workday -2.9%, ServiceNow -2.5%, Salesforce -2.1%) and rose under 1.5% after hours. A strong price reads as money available for that spending, which is these companies' revenue. That link is my inference.

Refiners closed lower than at midday (the bank's daily bars): CVR -11.2%, Delek -8.6%, Par, HF Sinclair and PBF about -7.2%, Valero and Marathon -5.5%, Phillips 66 -4.7%; Chevron -4.7%, Occidental -4.9%. themes.mechanism: A rising dollar and higher expected rates lower what holders pay for gold, which pays no interest.
